overview: Rentokil Initial is a UK-headquartered, dual-listed (LSE and NYSE ADR) global leader in pest control and hygiene & wellbeing services, operating in around 90 countries through two reporting regions, North America and International. The group was transformed by its October 2022 acquisition of Terminix, which made it the largest pest control operator in the US (the world's biggest pest control market), and it switched its reporting and functional currency from GBP to USD starting with the FY2025 Annual Report (FY2023/FY2024 comparatives were re-presented in USD; FY2019-FY2022 filings remain in GBP). In 2025 the group simplified its portfolio by divesting the France Workwear business, leaving Pest Control (~83% of revenue) and Hygiene & Wellbeing (~17%) as its two core categories.

business_model.summary: Rentokil earns recurring, contract-based revenue from route-based service visits (pest control treatments/monitoring and hygiene equipment servicing) performed by local technicians, supplemented by bolt-on M&A (30-40+ small acquisitions per year) that builds density in existing markets. Pest Control is now split into Pest Control Services and Business Services (product distribution, brand standards, lake/vegetation management) in North America. Growth is a mix of organic (pricing plus volume/new business) and acquired revenue, with organic growth normally reported at constant currency and excluding acquisitions.
business_model.customer_type: Mixed B2B and B2C: North America Residential and Commercial/National Accounts pest control, plus International commercial hygiene and pest contracts spanning food, hospitality, healthcare, and government customers
business_model.geographic_mix: North America ~62% of FY2025 revenue (Pest Control + small Hygiene & Wellbeing), International ~38% (88 countries across Europe, UK, Asia, Pacific, Latin America, MENAT and Sub-Saharan Africa)

main_competitors: Rollins Inc. (Orkin, Western Pest, Clark Pest Control)
Local/regional independent pest control operators (highly fragmented tail)
Cintas and other hygiene/washroom services providers (Hygiene & Wellbeing segment)
competitive_position.market_position: Largest pest control operator in North America by revenue following the Terminix acquisition, and a leading global player overall; Rollins (Orkin) is viewed by several analysts as the more operationally efficient North American competitor and has been taking share while Rentokil integrates Terminix. The US pest control market is estimated at roughly $25bn and highly fragmented, with over 30,000 operators, which favors scaled consolidators like Rentokil and Rollins.

moat_factors.description: National branch networks and route density lower cost-to-serve versus small independents, though 93% of operating profit comes from only the top 20 of 90 countries, implying the long tail of markets contributes little
Category-defining brands (Rentokil, Terminix, Initial, Ambius) plus ~30 retained regional/local pest brands representing over 90% of North America revenue support local trust and pricing power

Multi-year service contracts, termite warranties and recurring inspection cycles create retention (~82.6% group customer retention FY2025), though retention has been flat-to-only-slightly-improving in North America (80.4-80.7%)
Proprietary connected-device platforms (PestConnect, PestOptix, Lumnia) and the Branch 360 operating system differentiate the commercial offering and are being extended into AI-enabled monitoring
Licensing, pesticide-handling and safety regulation create some barrier to entry for commercial/national accounts work, but barriers are low for small residential operators

weaknesses: North America organic growth has persistently lagged the broader US pest control market (~6% market growth vs. low-single-digit Rentokil North America organic growth), implying ongoing share loss to Rollins and smaller competitors
Integration of Terminix (closed October 2022) remains unfinished four years on, with North America margins still below the now-abandoned 20%+ target and a complex multi-brand, multi-system structure
Highly fragmented end market limits pricing power at the low end and keeps bolt-on M&A as a structural, recurring cash use rather than a one-off
Legacy Terminix termite damage claim liabilities are an open-ended financial overhang (provision has grown, not shrunk, since acquisition)

growth_drivers: Secular tailwinds in pest control: urbanization, climate change (longer pest breeding seasons, pest range expansion), and tightening public health/sanitation regulation support above-GDP category growth
Hygiene & Wellbeing secular growth from rising health consciousness, workplace wellbeing focus and tightening hygiene regulation in International markets

North America turnaround initiatives under new CEO Mike Duffy (joined Feb/Mar 2026): customer focus, sales/operational excellence, and business simplification, including separating US Residential and Commercial leadership, a new Dallas regional head office/training center, and new North America (Rafa Carrasco) and Group Chief Transformation Officer (Matt Jochim, ex-McKinsey) hires

North America cost efficiency program: cumulative gross savings run-rate of ~$90m annualized as of H1 2026, targeted at ~$100m by 2027 (now being partly redeployed into growth investment rather than flowed straight to margin)
Continued bolt-on M&A in Pest Control and Hygiene & Wellbeing (36 deals in FY2025, ~$115m spend; ~$120m planned for 2026), concentrated in Growth and Emerging markets to build density

Digital/AI investment (Branch 360, PestConnect/PestOptix connected devices, Gemini AI rollout to ~63,400 colleagues, in-house 'RatGPT' AI agent platform) aimed at improving lead conversion, retention and field productivity
International Pest Control acceleration (Q2 2026 organic growth of 5.4%, up from 2.8% in Q1), with strong demand/pricing in UK, Southern Europe, Indonesia and India
Portfolio simplification post France Workwear divestiture frees capital and management attention for the two core categories and improves cash conversion (~100bps uplift cited by management)
Deleveraging: Net debt/EBITDA reduced to 2.4x in H1 2026, inside the 2.0-2.5x target range for the first time since the Terminix deal, creating capacity for further M&A or capital returns

business.description: Organic growth in North America Pest Control Services (2.6% H1 2026) continues to trail the ~6% US pest control market; management flagged weakening Residential lead flow into July 2026, and Commercial/National Accounts growth has been notably slower

Rollins (Orkin) and smaller independents are viewed by the market as taking share during Rentokil's prolonged Terminix integration; National Accounts retention requires dedicated remediation per management's own H1 2026 commentary

Legacy Terminix termite warranty provision increased to $384m at FY2025 and a further $47m addition in H1 2026 (closing provision $392m); driven by rising litigated claims, higher cost per claim, and an increase in the assumed long-term inflation rate from 2% to 3.2%; company explicitly states no guarantee claims trends or costs will improve

Company's own principal risk register rates 'failure to integrate acquisitions and execute disposals' as High and Stable, citing the scale of the ongoing Terminix integration alongside continuous bolt-on M&A activity

CEO Andy Ransom (12 years as CEO) retired and was succeeded by Mike Duffy (ex-OnTrac) in March 2026; new CFO-adjacent transformation and regional leadership hires (North America CEO, Chief Transformation Officer, Chief Marketing Officer) add execution/key-person risk during a critical turnaround phase

financial.description: Net debt of $3.575bn at H1 2026 (2.4x EBITDA) remains elevated post-Terminix; company targets 2.0-2.5x and issued its inaugural USD bond ($1.25bn across two tranches at 5.0%/5.625%) in 2025 at higher rates than legacy debt, raising interest costs ($222m cash interest FY2025 vs $181m FY2024)

Reporting currency changed from GBP to USD from FY2025; EUR and GBP-denominated bonds create translational FX exposure on net debt, and a strong dollar can mechanically dampen reported (AER) growth even when local-currency/organic trends are healthy
Argentina hyperinflation accounting has historically added volatility to adjusted interest, though the impact is shrinking ($3m FY2025 vs $9m FY2024)

regulatory.description: Trend toward non-toxic pest management and tightening rules on fumigants (e.g., sulfuryl fluoride) could restrict product/service options or raise compliance costs; company flags this as both an emerging strategic risk and a climate-transition risk
Operating in ~90 countries creates exposure to local labor, data privacy, anti-bribery, and tax authority challenges; Sarbanes-Oxley compliance applies given the NYSE ADR listing
EU Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive and UK Corporate Governance Code Provision 29 (effective 2026) add compliance costs and new disclosure obligations

macro.description: Residential pest control demand is somewhat discretionary and sensitive to consumer confidence/spending; Commercial demand tracks SME and corporate real estate activity
Business model is colleague-intensive (c.63,400 employees); tight labor markets raise wage costs and complicate recruitment/retention of technicians, especially during rapid branch expansion
Elevated net debt (~2.4x EBITDA) and the 2025 refinancing at higher coupons make the group moderately sensitive to prevailing rates on any further refinancing
Company specifically flagged Middle East conflict disruption to MENAT and softer Pacific comparatives as regional headwinds in Q1 2026

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global pest control market is described by management as growing at or above GDP, with the US market (roughly half of global pest control demand) growing around 6% per year; hygiene & wellbeing is similarly viewed as a resilient, largely non-discretionary, structurally growing category
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low-to-moderate; essential, contract-based, non-discretionary services for most commercial customers provide resilience, but residential demand and SME commercial activity have some sensitivity to consumer/business confidence
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - elevated leverage (2.4x net debt/EBITDA) post-Terminix and higher-coupon 2025 USD bond issuance mean refinancing and incremental debt costs are sensitive to rate levels

recent_developments.event: New leadership roles filled: North America CEO Rafa Carrasco started 3 August 2026; new North America Chief Marketing Officer Famous Rhodes (ex-Apex Service Partners) joined in July 2026; Group Chief Transformation Officer Matt Jochim (ex-McKinsey) appointed effective 7 September 2026, reporting to CEO
Company restructured into two operating divisions, North America and International, with Phil Wood named CEO of the International division

H1 2026 results: Group organic revenue growth 3.6% (North America 3.7%, International 3.5%), Adjusted Operating Profit +6.6% at CER, Free Cash Flow +12.8% to $318m (96% conversion), net debt/EBITDA improved to 2.4x (within 2.0-2.5x target range for first time since Terminix deal). Shares fell sharply (reported in a range of ~16-20%) after management retired the North America 20%+ operating margin target for 2027, choosing instead to reinvest cost savings into growth; weakening North America Residential lead flow into July was also flagged. Termite provision increased by a further $47m to $392m

Q1 2026 trading update: Group revenue +4.3% to $1,677m, organic growth 3.4%; North America organic growth 3.9% (Business Services +12.7%, Pest Control Services +2.8%); new CEO Mike Duffy's first public update noted 'continued momentum' but also flagged ongoing geopolitical uncertainty

FY2025 results (reported March 2026): Revenue $6,908m (+3.8% CER), organic growth 2.6% (North America 2.3%, International 3.0%), Adjusted Operating Profit $1,070m (+5.4%), Free Cash Flow $615m (+24.5%, 97.6% conversion), full-year dividend 12.39c (+3.0%). Mike Duffy appointed CEO Designate 16 February 2026, becoming CEO 16 March 2026, succeeding retiring Andy Ransom (12 years as CEO)

Completed sale of France Workwear business to H.I.G. Capital for enterprise value of €410m (net cash proceeds ~€397m/$397m), simplifying the portfolio to two core categories (Pest Control ~83%, Hygiene & Wellbeing ~17% of continuing revenue) and reducing capex/improving cash conversion
CEO Andy Ransom announced planned retirement ahead of the May 2026 AGM, triggering a board-led global CEO search

Issued inaugural USD bond ($1.25bn across two tranches: $750m 5-year at 5.0%, $500m 10-year at 5.625%), used to repay a maturing $700m term loan, raising average borrowing costs versus the retired facility

guidance.as_of: H1 2026 Interim Results (30 July 2026) and Q1 2026 Trading Update commentary carried forward

items.notes: Reiterated at both the April 2026 Q1 trading update and the July 2026 H1 results, despite noted weakness in North America Residential lead flow into July
H1 2026 conversion ran well ahead at 96%, management says still on track for above 80% for the full year

items.notes: Management is redeploying North America cost savings into growth investment rather than flowing them through to margin; no replacement quantitative target given, with more detail promised at FY26 results in February 2027

items.notes: H1 2026 cumulative gross savings of $45m, net savings after reinvestment of $28m; North America Pest Control Services margin improved to 19.7% in H1 2026 from 18.3% in FY2024

Updated from an earlier c.$200m technical guidance figure cited in the FY2025 annual report cash-flow guidance; H1 2026 commentary states 'around $120m' for 2026, focused on highest-opportunity markets/segments
Current estimate per H1 2026 release, up from the $95m actually paid in FY2025 and in line with management's prior statement of expecting 'a similar level' of cash payments in 2026
Achieved 2.4x at H1 2026, inside the target range for the first time since the Terminix acquisition

guidance.management_commentary: New CEO Mike Duffy: 'We have started to progress these priorities with a focus on North America... Achieving our potential will require disciplined reinvestment primarily back into the North America business which we will fully self-fund through cost savings. Our focus is driving volume growth over short-term margin expansion.' He also acknowledged 'we have seen some weakness in North America Residential lead flow towards the end of Q2 and into July,' while still expecting FY2026 profit in line with market expectations. The retirement of the 20% North America margin target in 2027 was explicitly linked to this redeployment of resources toward growth rather than margin.

bull_case: Structural, non-discretionary demand growth in pest control (~6% US market growth) and hygiene & wellbeing, driven by urbanization, climate change and tightening regulation, supports a long runway for above-GDP growth regardless of company-specific execution

Balance sheet has de-levered into the 2.0-2.5x target range (2.4x at H1 2026) for the first time since the Terminix deal, creating optionality for further bolt-on M&A or capital returns as free cash flow conversion runs ahead of guidance (96-98%)

New management team (CEO Mike Duffy plus new North America CEO, CMO and Group Chief Transformation Officer) brings fresh outside operating experience and a credible, well-telegraphed playbook (customer focus, sales/operational excellence, simplification) to finally close the growth gap to Rollins and the broader US market
International region is already executing well, with accelerating organic growth (3.5% H1 2026, Q2 at 4.2%) and healthy margins (19.1%), providing a stable earnings base while North America is fixed

Portfolio simplification (France Workwear divestiture) and cost-efficiency programs ($90m+ annualized North America savings run-rate) are structurally improving the quality and visibility of free cash flow, even before a North America growth recovery materializes
Highly fragmented end markets globally give Rentokil a long runway of accretive, de-risked bolt-on M&A to supplement organic growth
bear_case: North America, ~60% of group revenue, continues to underperform the underlying market four years after the Terminix deal closed, and management's own July 2026 commentary flagged fresh weakness in Residential lead flow going into H2 2026, raising doubts about the durability of any recovery

Abandonment of the 20%+ North America margin target for 2027 removes a key, long-standing valuation anchor and signals the turnaround will take longer and cost more than previously communicated, with no replacement target given until February 2027

Legacy Terminix termite damage claim provision keeps growing ($384m FY2025, up a further $47m to $392m at H1 2026) rather than stabilizing, with management explicitly disclaiming any guarantee that claim trends or costs will improve, implying an open-ended drag on cash flow and cost of the original acquisition
Elevated leverage and a 2025 refinancing at materially higher coupons (5.0-5.625% vs. legacy facilities) raise ongoing interest costs and reduce flexibility, even as leverage ratios have improved

Rollins (Orkin) is viewed by the market as the more efficient, faster-growing North American pure-play competitor, and continued relative share loss would undermine the core investment case for owning the larger, messier, multi-brand Rentokil/Terminix combination

Leadership and organizational churn (new CEO, new North America CEO, new CMO, new Chief Transformation Officer, and a divisional restructuring all within roughly six months) creates near-term execution risk and makes it harder for investors to isolate underlying trading performance from reorganization noise
